title: First Word All Beings Say Bismillah Through The Language Of Their State

questions.question: What question is asked at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: It asks whether all created things say “In the Name of Allah” in the way they are made and the way they act.

questions.question: What example is given to show that one person moving a whole town cannot be working by himself?
questions.answer: The example is of a man forcing all the people of a town to gather and work, which shows he must be acting with authority from a ruler.

questions.question: In that example, what would people understand about the man’s power?
questions.answer: They would understand that his strength is not just his own and that he is backed by the ruler and the state.

questions.question: How does that town example help explain the rest of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that when something very great is done, it points to a higher power behind it.

questions.question: What do tiny seeds and grains show us in this passage?
questions.answer: They show that small things can carry the start of huge trees, so they work by Allah’s power, not by themselves.

questions.question: What is the lesson about trees from this passage?
questions.answer: Trees receive gifts from Allah’s mercy and then give fruits and other benefits to people.

questions.question: How are gardens described in a way that helps us understand their blessings?
questions.answer: They are described like cooking places where many kinds of foods are prepared for people.

questions.question: Which animals are mentioned, and what do they provide?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats are mentioned, and they provide milk.

questions.question: Why is the milk of those animals described as a mercy?
questions.answer: It is pure, gentle, and nourishing, and it is given to people as a gift from Allah.

questions.question: What surprising thing do soft roots do?
questions.answer: They go through hard soil and even rock.

questions.question: What does the passage want us to understand from roots passing through hard ground?
questions.answer: It teaches that even weak-looking things can do hard tasks when Allah makes them able.

questions.question: What do leaves teach us by staying fresh in very hot weather?
questions.answer: They show that heat is also under Allah’s command.

questions.question: Who is criticized in the passage for trusting only in nature and physical causes?
questions.answer: People who explain things as if nature works by itself are criticized.

questions.question: Which two things are said to be under command, not acting on their own?
questions.answer: Hardness and heat are both under command.

questions.question: What is the main message of this whole passage?
questions.answer: Everything in creation works through Allah’s power and mercy, so we should see His control in all things.

questions.question: What claim from earlier is being checked again at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: The claim is that all beings say “In the Name of Allah” through how they are created and how they behave.

questions.question: How does the passage answer that claim?
questions.answer: It answers clearly that it is true.

questions.question: Why would a single person ordering around a whole town seem impossible by his own strength?
questions.answer: Because one person alone would not have enough power or authority to do that.

questions.question: If that person is really able to do it, whose support must he have?
questions.answer: He must have support from a ruler or government.

questions.question: What matching idea does the passage give about the created world?
questions.answer: It says that created things also act with Allah’s permission and power, not on their own.

questions.question: Why are seeds and grains strong signs of this truth?
questions.answer: Because something so tiny becomes the start of something huge, which shows amazing power beyond itself.

questions.question: What does the passage say trees do for us?
questions.answer: They bring out blessings and offer useful things like fruits and produce.

questions.question: How do gardens show generosity in this passage?
questions.answer: They produce many different foods as if they are preparing meals for people.

questions.question: What do the animals named in the passage have in common?
questions.answer: They are useful animals that give people wholesome milk.

questions.question: Why is the milk compared to something life-giving?
questions.answer: Because it is pure, beneficial, and a precious nourishment.

questions.question: What contrast is made between the roots and the ground?
questions.answer: The roots are soft and delicate, while the ground and rock are hard.

questions.question: What does this contrast help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove that the roots succeed by Allah’s command, not by their own strength.

questions.question: What two examples from prophets are used near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: One example is Musa striking the rock, and the other is Ibrahim being safe from fire.

questions.question: Why are those prophet examples mentioned here?
questions.answer: They help show that Allah can make hard things open and hot things lose their harm.

questions.question: What is the main question raised in the first line of the target passage?
questions.answer: It asks whether all things really declare Allah’s name by the way they function.

questions.question: What answer is given to that question?
questions.answer: The answer is that they truly do.

questions.question: What human example is used first to make the idea easier to understand?
questions.answer: The passage uses the example of one man making all the people of a town move and work.

questions.question: What would that example make you sure about?
questions.answer: It would make you sure that the man is using authority from above, not only his own strength.

questions.question: What does “not acting in his own name” mean in simple words here?
questions.answer: It means he is not working by his own independent power but as a representative of someone greater.

questions.question: How does the passage apply this idea to everything in creation?
questions.answer: It says all things do their work as signs of Allah’s power.

questions.question: What makes seeds and grains amazing in this passage?
questions.answer: They hold the beginning of very large trees even though they are tiny.

questions.question: According to the passage, where do trees get what they give?
questions.answer: They get it from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What picture is used for gardens to show how they serve people?
questions.answer: Gardens are pictured like cooking pots or kitchens making many kinds of food.

questions.question: What special gift do cows, camels, sheep, and goats provide?
questions.answer: They provide milk for people.

questions.question: What does this teach us about Allah as the Provider?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah sends pure and beneficial food through His creatures.

questions.question: What hard obstacle do roots go through?
questions.answer: They go through tough earth and rock.

questions.question: Why is it important that the roots are soft?
questions.answer: It makes the action more amazing and shows that the power behind them is from Allah.

questions.question: What do the leaves show by staying moist in strong heat?
questions.answer: They show that heat cannot overpower what Allah protects.

questions.question: What error of some thinkers is being challenged in this passage?
questions.answer: The error of thinking nature works by itself without Allah’s command is being challenged.

questions.question: What statement about all beings is repeated at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The statement is that all beings say “In the Name of Allah” through their condition and actions.

questions.question: What everyday-style example is used to help explain that statement?
questions.answer: An example is given of one man making a whole town’s people gather and work.

questions.question: Why would that man’s actions make people think of a king or government?
questions.answer: Because such large control would show that he has official backing.

questions.question: In the example, what is the man compared to?
questions.answer: He is compared to a soldier serving under higher authority.

questions.question: After this example, what big truth does the passage teach about all things?
questions.answer: It teaches that all things work under Allah’s authority.

questions.question: How do seeds and grains act as signs in this passage?
questions.answer: They show great results coming from very small beginnings.

questions.question: What do trees give people that shows mercy and care?
questions.answer: They give people useful produce and nourishment.

questions.question: How are gardens like places where food is prepared?
questions.answer: They bring forth many different foods as if meals are being made for us.

questions.question: Which animal products are focused on in the passage?
questions.answer: The passage focuses on milk from certain animals.

questions.question: What words best describe that milk from the passage’s meaning?
questions.answer: It is pure, gentle, and life-supporting.

questions.question: What unusual ability do roots and rootlets have?
questions.answer: They can enter and pass through very hard ground and stone.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens when Allah’s name is mentioned?
questions.answer: It says things become made obedient and manageable under His command.

questions.question: Which two parts of nature are especially said to be under command?
questions.answer: Rock-like hardness and burning heat are especially mentioned.

questions.question: How do the examples of roots and leaves answer people who only trust natural causes?
questions.answer: They show that the real control belongs to Allah, not to blind natural forces.

questions.question: What idea is the passage trying to prove right after the opening question?
questions.answer: It is trying to prove that all created things act in Allah’s name.

questions.question: What would you conclude if one person controlled a whole town by force?
questions.answer: I would conclude that he has authority and support from a ruler.

questions.question: Why is that conclusion reasonable?
questions.answer: Because one ordinary person would not be enough for such a huge task.

questions.question: What similar conclusion does the passage want us to make about the world?
questions.answer: It wants us to see that the works of creation come from Allah’s power.

questions.question: Why are seeds and grains mentioned before trees?
questions.answer: They show how something very small can be the beginning of something much bigger.

questions.question: What do trees receive and then pass on, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They receive blessings from Allah’s mercy and then pass them on to us.

questions.question: How do gardens help people, based on this passage?
questions.answer: They provide many kinds of foods for people.

questions.question: Why are cows, camels, sheep, and goats called blessed in this passage?
questions.answer: Because Allah gives people great benefit through them, especially milk.

questions.question: What does the milk example teach about Allah’s care for people?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah provides nourishing food in a gentle and merciful way.

questions.question: What is surprising about the roots of plants and trees?
questions.answer: Even though they are very soft, they can move through hard ground and rock.

questions.question: What does that surprise help us understand?
questions.answer: It helps us understand that physical weakness does not stop what Allah commands.

questions.question: What other delicate part of plants is mentioned besides roots?
questions.answer: The leaves are also mentioned.

questions.question: What do the leaves do that amazes the reader?
questions.answer: They stay fresh with moisture even during severe heat.

questions.question: What wrong idea is being pushed back against by these examples?
questions.answer: The idea that nature or material causes are in charge by themselves is being pushed back against.

questions.question: What teaching is asked about in the first sentence of the target passage?
questions.answer: It asks whether all beings really proclaim Allah’s name by their very state.

questions.question: Is the answer doubtful or certain in the passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as certain.

questions.question: What scene with a town is used to make the teaching easier to picture?
questions.answer: A scene is described where one man drives the people of a town somewhere and makes them work.

questions.question: What does that scene show about acting with authority?
questions.answer: It shows that big actions can point to hidden authority behind the one who appears in front.

questions.question: How is that like the way things work in nature?
questions.answer: The things we see are doing their work through Allah’s power behind them.

questions.question: Why are seeds and grains important examples?
questions.answer: Because they are tiny, yet they are connected to the growth of huge trees.

questions.question: What do trees do with the blessings given to them?
questions.answer: They bring them out and offer them for our benefit.

questions.question: What image does the passage use to describe gardens full of foods?
questions.answer: It uses the image of places where many foods are prepared.

questions.question: What common blessing comes from the animals listed in the passage?
questions.answer: A wholesome supply of milk comes from them.

questions.question: What does the milk example tell us about mercy?
questions.answer: It tells us that Allah sends tender and beneficial gifts to His creation.

questions.question: What can roots do that seems almost impossible?
questions.answer: They can push through hard earth and stone.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that the roots are soft like silk?
questions.answer: To make clear how amazing their work is and to show they are helped by Allah.

questions.question: What do leaves do during strong heat?
questions.answer: They keep their moisture and do not dry up as we might expect.

questions.question: What two natural forces are shown to be under Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: Hardness and heat are under Allah’s rule.

questions.question: What final lesson does the passage give about the created world?
questions.answer: The world is full of signs that everything obeys Allah and serves by His command.
